Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
711 AM EDT Sat Aug 15 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 215 AM EDT Saturday...

Increasing chances for 1" or greater rainfall in northern 
Vermont Sunday night into Monday morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 215 AM EDT Saturday...

1. Much of the weekend will be dry, then rain Sunday evening 
through the overnight hours is expected. 

2. Scattered showers on Monday will give way to another drier 
period Monday night into Tuesday. 

3. Near seasonable temperatures with a chance of showers mid to 
late next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 215 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure is building into the region today, 
which will maintain a slightly cooler than normal air mass with 
abundant dry air aloft. The low humidity pattern will flip beginning 
Sunday afternoon, and especially evening, as this high exits to our 
east and increasing moisture transport from the southwest occurs 
ahead of an occluding area of low pressure moving into the eastern 
Great Lakes. 

It continues to appear that weakly unstable air aloft will 
support moderate rainfall rates (as high as an inch/hour), and a
few rumbles of thunder at times. The heavier showers should 
tend to be at the nose of a strengthening nocturnal low level 
jet (850 millibar winds increasing to around 30 knots or so). 
The placement of the heavier rain is rather uncertain at this 
time and will tend to be wherever a north-south moisture 
gradient sets up overnight. The latest guidance shows a broad 
consensus in portions of northern/northeastern Vermont, but 
given large spread in recent forecast cycles of where heavier 
footprints of rain will fall we have maintained a blend showing 
roughly 0.5" of rain in much of our region. The event total 75th
percentile looks like reasonable higher end rainfall amounts, 
showing potential for swaths of rainfall in the 1-1.5" range in 
Vermont with less potential in the Adirondacks and points west. 
If heavier rain occurs farther south, the southwesterly low 
level flow will support locally heavier totals in the vicinity 
of the Green Mountain National Forest. Antecedent dry 
conditions and lack of a stationary boundary or setup for 
training showers are limiting factors for flash flood risk, such
that a marginal (level 1) excessive rainfall outlook looks 
reasonable for our region. The steady rain will exit to our east
towards Monday morning with the departure of isentropic lift 
and a broad area of surface low pressure into the region.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A deeper area of low pressure over northern Quebec will 
be dragging a weak cold front through the area during the day on 
Monday. In the wake of the early morning rain, there will be plenty 
of shallow moisture/elevated dew points such to support scattered to 
numerous showers during the day ahead of this front. Any modest 
heating will increase instability, although shallow cloud tops are 
expected due to a wedge of warm, dry air aloft and limit downpour 
intensity with low chances for thunder. As drier air continues to 
filter through on deepening west-northwesterly flow, rain chances 
will become orographically forced with otherwise increasing sunshine 
through the later part of the day.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Pretty much remain in a broad cyclonic flow that is 
dominating the Great Lakes-NY-New England. Heat ridge remains mainly 
across southern-southwest tier of CONUS. Our CWA is far enough from 
the periphery of the ridge that we stay largely influenced by 
the northern stream flow with seasonable temperatures and a 
chance of showers now and then. The best chance for showers will
be late Wed- Thu with a northern stream system.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 12Z Sunday...Fog will continue to lift between 12-13Z 
with mainly SKC today. Winds will become prevailing from the 
north-northwest less than 10 kts. 

Some higher clouds increase overnight with calm-light winds
again so some radiational fog possible again for KMPV, KSLK and
possibly KEFK. MVFR-IFR with fog with less LIFR as in the past
few mornings expected.

Outlook...

Sunday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Sunday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Definite SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
